title: Injectivity of a Boolean-indexed sum map
statement: Let $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be families of types indexed by $b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and for each $b$ let $g_b:\beta_b\to\gamma_b$ be an injective map. The map from pairs $(b,t)$ with $t\in\beta_b$ to pairs $(b,g_b(t))$ is injective.
hypotheses_covered: Families of types $\beta$ and $\gamma$ indexed by Boolean values
For each Boolean index $b$, the map $g_b:\beta_b\to\gamma_b$ is injective
replaced:
Let $\beta, \gamma : \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\} \to \mathrm{Type}$ be two
Boolean-indexed families of types and let $g_b : \beta_b \to \gamma_b$ be a map for each
$b \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$. If every $g_b$ is injective, then the map
$\Sigma_b\, \beta_b \to \Sigma_b\, \gamma_b$ sending $(b, t)$ to $(b, g_b(t))$ --- which
keeps the Boolean index and applies the family fibrewise --- is injective.
